 How to set up and use your my Social Security account
 Cassidy Horton · Contributing Writer Wed, November 11, 2026 at 8:00 AM CST 9 min read You can set up your my Social Security account by visiting SSA.gov/myaccount and selecting "Create an account with Login.gov" if you're in the U.S. or "Create an account with ID.Me " if you're abroad.  
 Once you're signed in, you can do several things, including ordering a replacement Social Security card, estimating benefits, changing your direct deposit, downloading important documents, and more. That way, you save time and minimize the need to call or visit a nearby office for help. 
 What is a my Social Security account? 
 A my Social Security account acts as your own personal dashboard on the Social Security Administration's official website, SSA.gov .  
 Your account allows you to:  
 Request replacement Social Security cards  
 Change your address 
 Update your direct deposit information 
 Print proof of benefits or tax forms 
 Review your Social Security statement 
 Estimate your benefits 
 Review your earnings history 
 Who can create a my Social Security account? 
 You can create an account if you're at least 18 years old, have a Social Security number, and have your own email address. 
 You don't need to be retired or receiving benefits. In fact, creating an account before retirement gives you time to check your earnings record and explore your future benefit estimates.  
 What you need before you start 
 You'll need these items to open a my Social Security account: 
 An email address you can access 
 Your Social Security number 
 A government-issued photo ID , such as a driver's license, state ID, or U.S. passport 
 A phone to receive a security code or to take photos of your ID 
 How to create your my Social Security account, step by step 
 Follow these steps to set up your own my Social Security Account. (Note: These instructions use Login.gov, which the SSA recommends for most people living in the United States.) 
 Visit SSA.gov/myaccount . Select "Create an Account with Login.gov ." You'll be redirected to the appropriate website. 
 Enter your email address. Follow the prompts to create an account with Login.gov or ID.Me . Then, check your inbox for a confirmation email.  
 Create a password. Choose something unique that you can remember or store safely. 
 Set up extra security. You'll be asked to choose an authentication method, such as receiving a code by text or phone call. This is called multi-factor authentication and helps protect your account. 
 Verify your identity. Follow the instructions to provide your Social Security number and photograph a U.S. driver's license, state ID, or passport book. You may also be asked for a selfie or to verify your phone number or mailing address. 
 Return to Social Security. Once verification is complete, follow the prompts to share your verified information with the SSA and accept its terms of service. 
 You should then arrive at your personal my Social Security account, where you can view your information and available services. 
 Having trouble with a step? The Login.gov Help Center explains how to handle verification problems, including situations where you can't use a smartphone. 
 Login.gov vs. ID.me: Which should you choose? 
 When you create or sign in to your my Social Security account, you'll see two options: Login.gov and ID.me . They're separate from the SSA, but both are approved for accessing your account. 
 If you already have an ID.me or Login.gov account, use whichever one you have to sign in to Social Security. There's no need to create a new account just for this. 
 If you live in the U.S. and have neither ID.Me or Login.gov , use Login.gov. It's what the SSA recommends for most U.S. users. 
 If you live outside the U.S. and don't have ID.Me or Login.gov , use ID.Me. It's what the SSA recommends for people living abroad. 
 Whichever you choose, you'll still access the same my Social Security services. 
 Important: As of June 7, 2025, you can no longer access your my Social Security account using just a username and password. You must log in through Login.gov or ID.Me for security purposes. If you used to have a username and password, you'll be asked to create an account with ID.Me or Login.gov before you can access your account again.  
 How to sign in to your my Social Security account 
 Once you've created your account, here's how to get back into it: 
 Go to SSA.gov/myaccount and select "Sign in here." 
 Choose Login.gov or ID.me , whichever you used when setting up your account. 
 Enter your email address and password. 
 Complete the security check. Depending on your settings, you may receive a code by text, phone call, or another authentication method. 
 Follow the prompts to return to your my Social Security dashboard. 
 What you can do with your my Social Security account 
 Your my Social Security account is a place to check your benefits and handle certain Social Security tasks without calling or visiting an office. What you can do depends on whether you're already receiving benefits. 
 If you're not receiving benefits yet, you can: 
 Estimate your retirement benefits. See how much you might receive each month if you retire at different ages. 
 Review your earnings history. Check whether the SSA has correctly recorded your past wages. Missing earnings could affect your future benefits. 
 Download your Social Security Statement. Get a summary of your earnings and estimated benefits. 
 If you're already receiving benefits, you may also be able to: 
 Check your payments. View benefit amounts and payment information. 
 Update your direct deposit. Change where eligible benefits are deposited. 
 Get important documents. Download a benefit verification letter or request a replacement SSA-1099 tax form. 
 Update your contact information. Change your mailing address or phone number when the service is available for your benefit type. 
 One tip: Even if retirement is years away, you may want to create a Social Security account to check your earnings record. The SSA recommends checking it for mistakes, so you're good to go when it's time to apply for benefits.

 How to read your Social Security Statement 
 Your Social Security Statement shows your earnings history and estimated future benefits. To find it, sign in at SSA.gov/myaccount, and look for "Your Social Security Statement" on your dashboard and select the option to view or download it. 
 If you don't have a Social Security account and are age 60 and older, the SSA will mail you a copy three months before your birthday. You can view a sample Social Security Statement here . 
 This statement shows you this key information: 
 Retirement benefit estimates: See what you might receive monthly if you start benefits at different ages, typically from 62 through 70. You can also see estimates for disability benefits and survivors benefits for a spouse and children.  
 Full retirement age: This is when you qualify for your full retirement benefit, based on your birth year. For people born in 1960 or later, it's 67. 
 Earnings record: Check that your reported wages and self-employment income look correct. These earnings help determine your benefits. 
 One tip: Your estimated benefits will likely change from year to year as new income gets recorded. If you notice missing or incorrect earnings, visit the SSA's earnings record correction page to learn how to request a correction. 
 How to get a benefit verification letter 
 A benefit verification letter is an official document showing whether you receive Social Security benefits and, if so, how much. You might need one when applying for housing, a loan, or financial assistance. 
 Here's how to get yours: 
 Sign in at SSA.gov/myaccount. 
 Find the "Benefit Verification Letter" option on your dashboard. 
 Follow the prompts to view, download, or print your letter. 
 The letter is free, and you can request one even if you don't currently receive benefits. In that case, it can confirm that you did not receive benefits. 
 How to keep your my Social Security account secure 
 Your Social Security account contains sensitive personal and financial information, so always take these precautions: 
 Use a unique password. Don't reuse one from another website. 
 Keep your security codes private. Never share a sign-in code with someone who calls or texts you unexpectedly. 
 Set up a backup security method. Login.gov recommends having at least two ways to verify your identity in case you lose your phone. 
 Watch for scams. For instance, Social Security would never threaten to suspend your number or demand payment to keep your benefits. These are likely scam attempts. 
 Troubleshooting common my Social Security account problems 
 This table highlights some common issues you may run into when trying to access a my Social Security account.  
 Problem 
 What to do 
 Forgot your password 
 Select the password recovery option on Login.gov or ID.me, whichever you use. 
 Not receiving a security code 
 Check that you're using the correct phone or authentication method. If you have a backup method, try it. 
 Can't verify your identity 
 Follow your sign-in provider's verification help instructions. If you still can't create an SSA account, contact your local Social Security office. 
 Lost access to your phone 
 Try your backup authentication method. If you have no backup, Login.gov may require you to delete and recreate your Login.gov account. 
 For sign-in help, visit Login.gov Help or the ID.me Help Center . 
 For Social Security account access or benefit questions, call 800-772-1213 (TTY: 800-325-0778), Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 7 p.m.  
 my Social Security account FAQs 
 Is a my Social Security account free? 
 Creating and using a my Social Security account is completely free. You should never have to pay to access your Social Security information online. 
 Who can create a my Social Security account? 
 Anyone age 18 or older with a Social Security number and a valid email address can generally create an account. You don't need to be retired or receiving benefits. 
 How do I check my Social Security account? 
 Visit SSA.gov/myaccount , select "Sign in here," and choose Login.gov or ID.me. Once you're signed in, you can review your benefits, earnings history, and other account information. 
 What should I do if I'm locked out of my Social Security account? 
 Start with the account recovery instructions from Login.gov or ID.me. If you still can't get in, contact Social Security at 800-772-1213 for help. 
 What's the difference between Login.gov and ID.me for my Social Security? 
 Both let you securely access your account. Login.gov is recommended for most people living in the U.S.; ID.me is recommended for people living abroad. 
 I had a my Social Security account before 2021. Do I need to create a new one? 
 You can still access your Social Security information, but you'll need to verify your identity and sign in through Login.gov or ID.me instead of using your old Social Security username and password.
